hypotheses.statement: Average total amount per yellow taxi trip on Monday 2025-01-20 was higher than on the other three Mondays in January 2025.
hypotheses.support_if: avg_total_amount on 2025-01-20 exceeds the mean of the three baseline Mondays by a meaningful margin (e.g., >5%).
hypotheses.refute_if: avg_total_amount on 2025-01-20 is within normal variation of the baseline Mondays.
hypotheses.status_reason: Avg total amount jumped +36.5% on 2025-01-20 vs baseline Mondays, well above the 5% threshold.

hypotheses.statement: Monday 2025-01-20 is Martin Luther King Jr. Day (federal holiday), while the other Mondays are regular weekdays, altering demand composition.
hypotheses.support_if: us_holidays shows a federal holiday on 2025-01-20 and none on the baseline Mondays.
hypotheses.refute_if: 2025-01-20 is not a federal holiday or baseline Mondays also have holidays.
hypotheses.status_reason: 2025-01-20 was MLK Day (federal holiday); baseline Mondays were not. Holiday aligns with the fare jump. Trip count is normal, suggesting composition change (e.g., more leisure/airport trips) rather than volume drop.

hypotheses.statement: Colder or snowier weather on 2025-01-20 increased fares via longer trips or surge-like effects.
hypotheses.support_if: tmax_c/tmin_c are lower or snow_mm higher on 2025-01-20 vs baseline Mondays, and avg_trip_distance is higher.
hypotheses.refute_if: Weather is similar or warmer/drier on 2025-01-20, or avg_trip_distance does not increase.
hypotheses.status_reason: Cold non-holiday weekdays in Jan 2025 (Q7: 2025-01-06, -08, -16, -21, -22, -23) show normal avg_total_amount (~$25–27.6) despite tmax_c ≤ -1°C. 2025-01-06 was cold (-1.0°C) with normal fare. The jump on 2025-01-20 is not explained by cold alone; holiday is the differentiator.

hypotheses.statement: Trip distance increased on 2025-01-20, mechanically raising fares.
hypotheses.support_if: avg_trip_distance on 2025-01-20 is materially higher than baseline Mondays.
hypotheses.refute_if: avg_trip_distance is flat or lower on 2025-01-20.
hypotheses.status_reason: Avg trip distance on 2025-01-20 (4.79 mi) did not increase vs baseline Mondays (4.40, 5.53, 4.52 mi). Fare jump occurred without a distance increase, ruling out longer trips as the cause.

hypotheses.statement: Holiday shifted trip mix toward airport/long-haul zones (higher fare per mile), raising average fare without distance change.
hypotheses.support_if: avg_total_amount rises while avg_trip_distance is flat, implying higher fare-per-mile on 2025-01-20.
hypotheses.status_reason: Daily aggregates lack zone detail. Avg distance did not rise with fare, weakening the zone-mix proxy, but airport/Manhattan core shifts could still occur without distance change (e.g., tolls, surcharges). Cannot confirm or refute without zone-level data.

hypotheses.statement: Holiday surcharges, tolls, extra charges, or higher tips drove the fare jump on 2025-01-20.
hypotheses.support_if: Fare-component averages (tolls_amount, extra_charges, tip_amount, fare_amount) on 2025-01-20 exceed baseline Mondays.
hypotheses.refute_if: All fare-component averages are in line with baseline Mondays.
hypotheses.status_reason: Trip count is normal (c3), but fare-component breakdown (tolls, surcharges, tips) was not queried. A component anomaly (e.g., holiday surcharge, toll changes) could drive the fare jump without volume or distance changes. Needs fare-component test.
